edits.text: PARTIES. This Lease is between Calder Properties as Landlord and [Tenant’s full legal name, entity type and jurisdiction—to be confirmed] as Tenant.

2. RENT. Tenant shall pay monthly Base Rent of [amount—to be confirmed]. Base Rent shall commence only when Landlord delivers possession of the premises to Tenant in the agreed delivery condition specified in [delivery specifications—to be agreed]. No Base Rent shall accrue before that delivery. The parties shall confirm the delivery date in writing.

3. TERM; RENEWAL. The initial term is sixty months commencing on [Commencement Date—to be confirmed]. Tenant shall have one option to renew for an additional [number] months by written notice delivered at least [number] months before expiration of the initial term, provided no material Tenant default remains uncured beyond the applicable notice and cure period at exercise or commencement of the renewal term. Renewal Base Rent shall be [amount or determination mechanism—to be agreed]; all other lease terms shall continue, except that no further renewal option is granted.

4. ASSIGNMENT AND SUBLETTING. Tenant shall not assign this Lease or sublet any part of the premises without Landlord’s prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. No consent is required for an assignment or sublease to an entity controlling, controlled by or under common control with Tenant, or for a transfer in connection with a bona fide sale of Tenant’s business or reorganization. Tenant shall give Landlord reasonable written notice of any exempt transfer and supporting information reasonably necessary to establish the exemption. Any assignee shall assume Tenant’s obligations under this Lease in writing. No transfer shall release Tenant from its obligations absent Landlord’s express written agreement.

5. NOTICE AND CURE. Before exercising remedies for a Tenant default, Landlord shall give written notice describing the default and allow Tenant ten business days after receipt to cure a monetary default and thirty days after receipt to cure a nonmonetary default. If a nonmonetary default cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, Tenant shall have such additional time as is reasonably necessary, provided Tenant begins cure within that period and diligently pursues completion. These provisions do not prevent lawful emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect persons or property.
